title: The passive voice
description: Say what was done, without saying who did it.
grammarNote: The passive is ser plus the participle: el cuadro fue pintado por Ana.

explanation.summary: Spanish has a passive voice for the same reason English does: sometimes the action matters more than the doer. The structure is ser plus the participle, and it needs a por to say who did it.

sections.heading: Ser and the participle
sections.body: The participle is the -ado or -ido form: pintado, escrito, hecho. The tense goes on ser, not on the participle: el cuadro fue pintado, the painting was made. If you do not say who did it, you do not need por at all: el cuadro fue pintado, and that is a complete sentence.

examples.es: El cuadro fue pintado por Ana.
examples.en: The painting was done by Ana.

sections.heading: When to use it
sections.body: The passive is for when the doer is unknown, obvious or unimportant, and for a polite way of saying who did something: ha sido recompensado por el comité. It is much more common in writing than in speech.

examples.es: Se ha publicado un nuevo libro.
examples.en: A new book has been published.
He was honoured by the committee.
